LAG positive: Reitsma bivariate model meta-analysis (sensitivity, specificity)



Methods

Statistical analyses were performed using RC MetaStudio (version 0.6.0; Research Consultancy) [1] with the R package mada (version 0.5.12) [2]. Sensitivity and specificity were jointly modeled using the Reitsma bivariate model [3, 4, 5].

Results

In total, 3 studies were included; 14 studies were excluded. The summary sensitivity was 75.73% (95% CI 63.10% to 85.06%). The summary specificity was 93.95% (95% CI 53.11% to 99.53%). The summary false-positive rate was 6.05% (95% CI 0.47% to 46.89%). In Sensitivity, the 95% prediction interval was 56.42% to 88.26%. In Specificity, the 95% prediction interval was 9.73% to 99.96%. In False-positive rate, the 95% prediction interval was 0.04% to 90.27%.

Sensitivity and specificity were jointly modeled using the Reitsma bivariate model [3, 4, 5]. A continuity correction of 0.5 was applied to all studies if any zero exists.
Results
In total, 17 studies were included. The summary sensitivity was 65.762% (95% CI 59.020% to 71.923%). The summary specificity was 80.975% (95% CI 73.885% to 86.492%). The summary false-positive rate was 19.025% (95% CI 13.508% to 26.115%). In Sensitivity, the 95% prediction interval was 49.071% to 79.292%. In Specificity, the 95% prediction interval was 49.292% to 94.907%. In False-positive rate, the 95% prediction interval was 5.093% to 50.708%.
